---
title: "04 — Develop models using earlier years only"
output: html_notebook
---

**Measures:** out-of-time model discrimination (weighted AUROC) and probability error (weighted Brier score) on annual forward-validation folds. Models never train on the same or a later year than their fold assessment.


## Setup

Loads the unchanged input settings, shared model functions, and the persistent run
increment. The output suffix identifies this run.

```{r setup}
# Set the project root, then load R code from the shared R Notebooks.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Search upward for the project marker so notebook paths do not depend on a particular
# subfolder.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    # Walk toward the filesystem root until the project marker is found.
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        # Move up one directory; an unchanged parent marks the filesystem root.
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook execution root
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolve the project before loading modules; configure subsequent knitr chunks to use
# that root.
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract R chunks in source order and evaluate them in the caller environment.
# This lightweight loader does not process chunk options such as eval = FALSE.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    text <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(text, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(text) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        # Use the next standalone closing fence for this R chunk.
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing code or closing fence in ", path)
        }
        paste(text[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared settings and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration before helpers, retaining the existing presentation palette module.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Existing-run attachment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Attach to an allocated run rather than incrementing the counter in this stage.
run_context <- attach_run()
cat("[RUN] Current increment:", run_context$id, "\n")
```


## Evaluate forward validation folds

Compares weighted logistic regression, LASSO logistic regression, and random forest. The
best tuning setting for each family is chosen by the mean Brier score over validation
years.

```{r evaluate-forward-validation-folds}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Forward-year model development
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Train on years strictly earlier than each assessment year.
# Compare tuning settings using mean fold Brier error, without using 2023–2025 outcomes
# here.

check_packages(c("glmnet", "ranger", "Matrix"))
training <- load_run_rds("checkpoints", "02_development")
settings <- list(
    logistic = NA_real_,
    lasso = lasso_lambdas,
    forest = forest_mtry
)
results <- list()
index <- 0L


# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (year in cv_test_years) {
    # Exclude the assessment year and all later years from this fold training set.
    earlier <- training[YEAR < year]
    # Evaluate only the held-out survey year for this fold.
    assessment <- training[YEAR == year]
    if (!nrow(earlier) || !nrow(assessment)) {
        stop("Empty forward-validation fold for ", year)
    }
    cat("[TEMPORAL CV] Training before ", year, "; evaluating ", year, "\n", sep = "")

    for (family in names(settings)) {
        for (parameter in settings[[family]]) {
            index <- index + 1L
            set.seed(seed + year + index)
            fitted <- fit_classifier(family, earlier, parameter)
            probabilities <- predict_classifier(fitted, assessment)
            measurements <- weighted_metrics(
                assessment$FMD, probabilities, assessment$train_weight
            )
            results[[index]] <- data.frame(
                assessment_year = year,
                family = family,
                setting = if (is.na(parameter)) "default" else as.character(parameter),
                measurements
            )
            rm(fitted)
            gc(verbose = FALSE)
        }
    }
}
all_folds <- data.table::rbindlist(results)
summary <- all_folds[, .(
    folds = .N,
    mean_brier = mean(brier),
    mean_auc = mean(auc, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = .(family, setting)][order(mean_brier)]
# Select the lowest mean Brier error separately within each model family.
chosen <- summary[, .SD[which.min(mean_brier)], by = family]

if (any(!is.finite(chosen$mean_brier))) {
    stop("Temporal validation returned invalid model selection scores")
}

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(all_folds, "04_annual_forward_folds")
save_table(summary, "04_tuning_summary")
save_table(chosen, "04_chosen_settings")

# Persist this run-specific object for downstream stages without intentionally
# overwriting an existing artifact.
save_once_rds(
    stats::setNames(as.list(chosen$setting), chosen$family),
    "checkpoints",
    "04_tuning"
)
print(summary)
```


## Visualize out-of-time performance

Displays the AUROC achieved for each model family on each held-out historical year. A
lower value means poorer classification discrimination, not necessarily a higher
false-negative rate at every threshold.

```{r visualize-out-of-time-performance}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Selected tuning settings across folds
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Restrict the display to the chosen setting within each model family.
# The plotted fold results also informed tuning; they are not a separate final test.

# Plot only the eventual tuning winner for each family in each fold.
plot_data <- merge(
    all_folds[, .(assessment_year, family, setting, auc)],
    chosen[, .(family, setting)],
    by = c("family", "setting")
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Build the chart using the existing palette and theme; retain the original scales and
# labels.
plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_data,
    ggplot2::aes(assessment_year, auc, color = family)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::geom_point() +
    atg_scale_color_models() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Forward-year model discrimination",
        subtitle = "Development years only; higher weighted AUROC is better",
        x = "Held-out survey year",
        y = "Survey-weighted AUROC",
        color = "Model"
    )
show_and_save(plot, "04_forward_auroc", 9, 5)
```
